edbDesc: Hysteresis phenomena occur in magnetic and ferromagnetic materials, as well as in the elastic, electric, and magnetic behavior of materials, in which a lag occurs between the application and the removal of a force or field and its subsequent effect. Magnetic field hysteresis loss causes heating. This effect is used in induction cooking, where an alternating magnetic field causes a ferrite container to heat directly rather than being heated by an external heat-source.
title: Magnetic hysteresis
description: Iron remembers: magnetise it and switch the field off and some magnetism stays, and to undo it you must push the other way; push hard enough and it stops responding at all (saturation). Emil Warburg measured this loop in 1880 and James Ewing, working in Japan, named it hysteresis a few years later.
effect: a magnetic material keeps some magnetism after the field is removed
strength: A neodymium magnet resists being unmagnetised by fields of about a tesla, while soft transformer iron flips with a field tens of thousands of times weaker.
pickWhy: Borderline: Specific effect behind magnetic memory; credit is split between Warburg (first loop, 1880) and Ewing (named it, 1880s); picked Warburg.
